name: Cheesy & Spicy Ramen Hot-Pot with Ham, Shrimp & Soup Dumplings
description: A bubbling spicy-cheesy ramen hot-pot loaded with ham, shrimp, soup dumplings, mushrooms, greens and eggs.

source.note: The Reel did not expose a reliable written recipe. Quantities and method are Food Expert-developed.

ingredients.name: Ottogi Cheesy Spicy Ramen or similar cheesy spicy Korean stir-fry ramen

steps.title: Prepare ingredients
steps.text: Slice the ham, mushrooms and green onions. Pat the shrimp dry. Keep soup dumplings frozen until cooking.

steps.title: Build the hot-pot broth
steps.text: In a wide pot, combine water, milk, butter, garlic and gochujang. Bring to a gentle simmer; do not hard-boil the dairy.

steps.title: Cook dumplings and mushrooms
steps.text: Add frozen soup dumplings and mushrooms. Simmer gently until the dumplings are heated through. Avoid aggressive boiling so the wrappers stay intact.

steps.title: Add ramen
steps.text: Add ramen noodles and their seasoning/sauce packets. Cook according to the package, stirring occasionally to separate the noodles.

steps.title: Add ham and shrimp
steps.text: Add ham and shrimp near the end. Cook until the shrimp are opaque and firm and the dumplings are hot throughout.

steps.title: Make it cheesy
steps.text: Reduce heat to low. Add processed cheese and mozzarella. Stir gently until melted and creamy. Add chili oil or chili crisp to taste.

steps.title: Add greens
steps.text: Add bok choy or pechay and cook just until wilted but still slightly crisp.

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.text: Crack eggs into separate spaces in the broth. Cover and cook until whites are set and yolks are soft, or longer for firmer yolks.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Top with green onions and sesame seeds. Drizzle with additional chili oil or chili crisp. Serve immediately from the heat-safe pot.

donenessCues: Shrimp are opaque and firm, not rubbery.
Dumpling wrappers remain intact and the centers are hot.
Noodles are tender but not mushy.
Cheese is fully melted into a creamy broth.
Egg whites are set to the desired doneness.
chefNotes: Keep the dairy at a gentle simmer and add cheese near the end to reduce the chance of separation.
Frozen soup dumplings should go in frozen and be cooked gently so they do not split.
Pechay is a practical CDO/Philippine substitute for bok choy.
The dish is richest when served immediately while the cheese is hot and fluid.
commonMistakes: Breaking the soup dumplings with vigorous stirring
substitutions: Any Korean cheesy/spicy instant ramen can replace Ottogi.
Evaporated milk can replace whole milk, though the broth will taste richer.
Frozen shrimp can be used after thawing and drying well.
storage: For best quality, eat immediately. If leftovers remain, refrigerate promptly in a covered container and reheat gently until thoroughly hot. Noodles and dumplings will soften during storage.
